comparison: Halve the Cartesian mesh spacing at unchanged biological inputs and numerical time steps, with same seed labels. The stochastic event history can change.
findings: Both additional runs exited zero and reached 96 h. The accepted N3 group has 291 hourly states; the two new runs passed 198 all-field states and 392 ledger rows. The frozen runner omitted only the optional standalone exit sidecar for the last child; unchanged per-case and aggregate execution records retain its actual zero return code.

Fine-grid 96 h residual target counts are 192, 202 and 195, compared with original same-seed counts of 146, 144 and 119. All fine-grid endpoints exceed the entire original N3 endpoint range. The descriptive ranges are not confidence intervals.

Time-averaged live-target counts decrease from 456.0417, 476.3021 and 475.1823 to 382.0208, 406.2396 and 403.5156. Paired changes are -74.0208, -70.0625 and -71.6667 targets, despite higher final residual counts. Every full paired trajectory crosses: mean absolute differences are 83.2500, 83.2083 and 91.3125, with hourly maxima of 157, 157 and 179 targets.

The prespecified primary screen flags 49, 41 and 45 metrics, including 13, 11 and 11 count entries. Thirty-eight entries are common to all seeds and have consistent nonzero same-seed signs. These include early target and antigen-positive population changes, later effector counts and late IFNG/TNF readouts. IFNG and TNF are identical fields here, so duplicated field entries do not establish independent mechanisms.

Fine-grid local-entry minus fine-grid 2D time-averaged differences are -15.8125, +1.6302 and +5.5469 targets, compared with +43.8542, +74.0729 and +80.7865 in the original configurations. The original positive integral ordering is not retained across the refined N3 group. The first negative seed does not establish a stable reversed ordering; the refined signs are mixed.

At 96 h the fine-grid local-entry scenario still has 120, 123 and 123 more targets than fine-grid 2D, and 127, 126 and 126 more than fine-grid 3D. Its time-averaged excess over fine-grid 3D remains positive: 26.6510, 48.1042 and 47.9479. All six comparative trajectories cross, so this is not an ordering at every time.

The fine-grid endpoint contains one assigned antigen-positive target in seed 0 and none in seeds 1 and 2, compared with 10, 22 and 8 in the original local-entry runs. Unprimed residual counts are 3, 0 and 2. All remaining target states and the different direction of integral versus endpoint effects are retained.

At 48 h, initial-hull occupancy fractions decrease in all seeds by 0.1351, 0.0353 and 0.0258, while sphere-contact counts rise by 37, 54 and 56. Saved live-target links change by -10, -7 and 0. These are distinct spatial observables; occupancy cannot substitute for contacts or assigned target-link states. First saved positive access/activity times are unchanged, which does not resolve sub-hour event timing.

The N3 followup confirms material mesh dependence in populations, fields and spatial readouts. It does not establish quantitative grid convergence. Neither a universal local-entry-versus-2D integral ordering nor the opposite ordering is supported. Conditional comparisons must specify the configuration, numerical setting, time summary and sampled seeds.
remaining_decision: Complete claim-specific synthesis of all ten N3 numerical groups and three single-seed screens. Persistent flags are interpreted here but no positive numerical gate is inferred. Any further simulation requires a concrete retained-claim gap and a bounded prior decision.
